title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions for Neural Invariants
abstract: arXiv:2606.07627v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A representation transfers if it stays usable once the task has changed. Standard evaluations report target accuracy or a distance between data distributions, but neither says which structure of the representation is meant to survive. Here we make that structure explicit and computable. A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor, and a representation is a functor into a category of invariants. The structure the target has to exhibit is the left Kan extension of the source functor along the change of task. Our transfer discrepancy is the supremum over target objects of the distance between that extension and the observed target invariant, so we score transfer against the invariant the change of task forces rather than against the source. translated_title: 学习迁移：神经不变量的Kan扩展
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.07627v3 公告类型：替换 摘要：如果表示在任务改变后仍然可用，则称其具有迁移性。标准评估报告目标准确性或数据分布之间的距离，但两者都没有说明表示的哪种结构旨在存续。在这里，我们使这种结构明确且可计算。任务是一个小范畴，任务的改变是一个函子，表示是进入不变量范畴的函子。目标必须展现的结构是源函子沿任务改变得到的左Kan扩展。我们的迁移差异是目标对象上该扩展与观测到的目标不变量之间距离的上确界，因此我们根据任务改变所强制的不变量来评分迁移，而非根据源。我们证明了在逗号范畴、链复形和持久模块中扩展的余核表示。在有限类型的一参数模块上，我们展示了该差异。
tldr: 本文通过范畴论中的Kan扩展形式化定义了表示迁移所需保持的结构，并提出了一种新的迁移差异度量，以任务改变所强制的不变量为目标进行评分。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes the structure that representations must preserve during transfer using Kan extensions from category theory, and proposes a new transfer discrepancy metric scored against the invariant forced by the task change.
